scope: Delivery playbooks (epic cr-p3em: cr-p3em.1, .2, .3): Visual parity, Babysit and Shipping built as adapted playbooks, routed from mvp-mode. No report and no upstream trait rows (README 4a's playbook exemption).
method: Owner ruling 2026-11-20 to build all three adapted, and the owner's answers to the adaptation's four questions (all as recommended; verdicts posted on both the pull request and its bead). Each adopt-merged supersedes the matching 2026-11-20-deferred-playbooks defer.

subject: doc:.claude/skills/mvp-mode/playbooks/visual-parity.md
why: New playbook, owner ruling of 2026-11-20. Steps: (1) a baseline of every component on one surface before any migration, building the harness through build-a-lever when there is none; (2) shared primitives first, blocking; (3) one component at a time, image diff against its baseline on its surface, systematic-debugging for an unclear delta, delegation only when the owner asks for parallel work; (4) land, and pr when the request asks for a pull request; (5) closeout on every exit. Gates: the frozen baseline and the zero-difference rule.

subject: cursor_plugins:playbook:pstack/skills/poteto-mode/playbooks/visual-parity
why: Map 2.10 and the owner ruling of 2026-11-20: build it for projects that have a user interface; the owner's answer 4 makes any pixel difference a failure unless the request sets a tolerance.

modifications: Any pixel difference fails unless the owner sets a tolerance in the request (owner answer 4).
No harness: building one through build-a-lever is the first step.
The project's own visual harness or verify skill drives the surface, in place of a vendor control skill.
Parallel worktrees, one owner per component, only when the owner asks, through delegation and principle-separate-before-serializing-shared-state.
Opening a pull request becomes land, and pr only when the request asks for one; a closeout on every exit keeps the harness and baseline.
deliberately_dropped: The loop command per component: the step repeats until no difference, with no tool name (ruling 12). revisit_when: never for the name.
Parallel worktrees by default: they run only when the owner asks. revisit_when: the owner rules parallel by default.

subject: doc:.claude/skills/mvp-mode/playbooks/babysit.md
why: New playbook, owner ruling of 2026-11-20. Steps: (1) the bead's claim as the single-watcher lock; (2) the forge's merge state and the order conflicts, threads, checks; (3) threads through review feedback mode, real findings fixed red-first in the owning pull request; (4) a failing check classified before any rerun; (5) land, one push wave, replies from files; (6) a bounded wait on gh pr checks --watch, wake only for a named deadline; (7) closeout on every exit. Gates: the declared mode, the merge frontier, frozen topology, the owner's push-and-reply grant in drive and threads-only, and never merging.

subject: cursor_plugins:playbook:pstack/skills/poteto-mode/playbooks/babysit
why: Map 2.14 and the owner ruling of 2026-11-20: watch our own pull requests to merge-ready with failure classification before any retry; the owner's answer 1 grants pushing fixes and replying on threads in drive and threads-only.

modifications: gh is the only forge; readiness is read from gh pr view (state, mergeable, mergeStateStatus, reviewDecision, baseRefName) and gh pr checks, with no watcher script.
Waiting is a bounded background gh pr checks --watch with the platform's notice; wake only for a deadline the request names.
One babysitter per stack is the bead's claim.
Review comments go through review in feedback mode; real findings are fixed red-first through tdd; replies are written to a file and published from it.
Owner grant (answer 1): in drive and threads-only, push fix commits to the pull request's own branch and reply on its threads without asking each time; never merge, rebase or force-push.
A recurring dismissal pattern is proposed as a lesson where AGENTS.md sends lessons, in place of a shared bot rubric.
deliberately_dropped: The Origin forge and Graphite: gh only. revisit_when: a project uses another forge.
The watch-pr script, its verdict names (READY, WAITING, ADVANCE, COMPLETE) and the frozen queued-stack list: the forge's own state replaces them. revisit_when: a project needs merge-queue watching.
The loop command: a bounded background wait replaces it (ruling 12).
The sanctioned follow-up pull request when a fix's owner has merged: opening one is outside the owner's grant, so it is reported. revisit_when: the owner widens the grant.
Bot pass counts and leaning toward dismissal from the third pass: bot-specific. revisit_when: a review bot runs on our pull requests.
Autopilot owners rebasing their own branch: the Autopilot playbooks are not built yet. revisit_when: they are built.

subject: doc:.claude/skills/mvp-mode/playbooks/shipping.md
why: New playbook, owner ruling of 2026-11-20. Steps: (1) an older verdict rechecked by patch-id at the current head; (2) a verifier that did not write the change runs it as a user would, through delegation's reviewer role, each verdict posted on the pull request and its bead; (3) the verified run merged bottom-up one at a time and read back, auto-merge only on a covered head, the next pull request retargeted and pushed with lease under the grant; (4) closeout on every exit, closing each landed bead with the read-back when its acceptance holds. Gates: the owner's merge grant, the contiguous verified run and hands off while landing.

subject: cursor_plugins:playbook:pstack/skills/poteto-mode/playbooks/shipping
why: Map 2.15 and the owner ruling of 2026-11-20: land a pull request or stack bottom-up, reusing verdicts by patch-id; the owner's answers 2 and 3 set the merge grant and post each verdict on both the pull request and its bead.

modifications: The verifier is a delegation reviewer from another model family, running the change the way the project runs it, in place of vendor cloud agents and control skills.

Owner grant (answer 2): a request to ship or land authorizes merging the verified run and, for a stack, retargeting the next pull request to trunk and a push with --force-with-lease on its own branch when its parent lands; nothing else.
Owner answer 3: each verdict (PASS, PASS+NOTES or FAIL, with head SHA and patch-id) is posted from a file as a comment on the pull request and on its bead.
A patch-id match keeps a verdict; any difference needs a fresh verdict.
Added: after a merge is read back, the bead is closed with that evidence when its acceptance holds, or commented and left open.
gh only; the merge method is the repository's own.
deliberately_dropped: The Origin forge and Graphite: gh only. revisit_when: a project uses another forge.
The noise analysis that keeps a lane's result when patches differ only in tests, docs or lint: any difference re-verifies. revisit_when: re-verification cost blocks landings.
Moving an independent verified pull request onto trunk to land alone: that retarget is outside the owner's grant. revisit_when: the owner widens the grant.
The queued watcher script and the loop command: a bounded background gh pr checks --watch replaces them (ruling 12).

subject: ours:mvp-mode
why: Router lines for Babysit, Shipping and Visual parity, each naming the neighbour it must not take: Babysit never merges and sends a merge request to Shipping; Shipping is not land; Visual parity is not prototype or refactoring. The catalog is unchanged (no new skill).
